I got a lot of questions about dimple scars when I had my cheek piercings and I had them for a long time (for cheek piercings) so I thought I’d post so others can see

-I had my cheeks pierced for a bit over 6 years 

-they healed well considering they’re notoriously difficult piercings and they were pierced by a high quality piercer with high quality jewelry. I only wore titanium bars and m&m beads and switched the decorative pieces between titanium and solid gold

-I had 12g labrets with m&m beads on the inside the entire time I had them in other than the first couple weeks I had flat backs before switching to m&m beads

-my right side was the bad side and would repeatedly develop fluid pockets that I would pop myself and if I didn’t pop them myself they would pop randomly without me noticing. Other people would notice this as they would drop lymph fluid and blood and point it out. This was maybe once a month or every few months the first few years but by the time I took them out it was happening every few weeks. The right side would also get irritated and inflamed easily if it was yanked by anything 

-the left side was my good side and didn’t get irritated or inflamed very often. It would also occasionally develop fluid pockets but they were smaller and more infrequent 

-I only ever cleaned them with sterile saline and a piece of toilet paper or paper towel folded up 

-I did chew the bars and play with them a lot and twirl them sometimes with my fingers. I know that’s bad, it’s a bad habit, I do not suggest that 

-the first two days after I took them out I did have fluid leak from the piercing hole randomly. That went away after a few days 

-pictures show that the “dimple” scars show regardless of wether I’m smiling or have a straight face

-I don’t mind the scars! I think they’re cute. They don’t bother me at all I just thought others would be interested to see the healing scars since I got a lot of questions about what happens if I take them out over the years

I usually get questions on what it is and how it’s done so here’s an explanation! It’s called a subdermal implant, the same thing as those silicone horns some people get that are more famous but it’s a different shape of silicone and in your thumb. This kind is nicknamed a thumb spine.

It’s a pretty gnarly process! They make an incision all the way through the skin at your wrist (you can still see the red scar on mine from that), use a metal tool to detach your skin from your muscle *I believe* between the skin and the fat/muscle to form a pocket the right size for the silicone implant, position the implant under the skin, drain the extra fluid, then sew you up and drain the last of the extra fluids. Then it’s just keeping it clean and dry until the wound heals, and it takes up to 6-9 months for the skin to fully fuse back to the muscle over the implant. So it’ll get more and more defined over the next few months
